summary: A leafy Lanna-style restaurant in Chang Phueak for a relaxed meal built around Northern Thai shared dishes. Michelin lists it at ฿฿ and recommends spicy galangal dip with steamed mushrooms and spicy vegetable soup with snake-head fish.
whyGo: Try several regional dishes in a sit-down garden setting, with indoor air-conditioned tables and private pavilions.
A good way to sample Northern Thai specialties such as nam phrik, herby soups, and classic curry dishes rather than choosing only one noodle bowl.
bestFor: A small group sharing multiple dishes; Michelin describes it as family friendly.
Visitors who enjoy savory, herb-forward Northern Thai cooking and can ask staff to adjust or explain spice where possible.
skipIf: You need a reliably vegetarian, vegan, halal, or allergen-controlled meal: the menu includes fish and meat, and ingredient or cross-contact details are not published.
You need confirmed step-free access, accessible toilets, or a quiet indoor table; these facilities are not documented.
duration: Allow about 60–90 minutes for a meal (planning estimate; busy periods may take longer).
cost: Michelin lists ฿฿; a recent Wongnai menu lists examples including muang appetizer platter ฿163, gaeng hung lay ฿98, and sai ua ฿93. Treat these as indicative only and confirm current menu prices. For a shared meal, budget roughly ฿200–400 per person (planning estimate, depending on dishes and drinks).
hours: Michelin currently lists Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri and Sun 11:00–21:00; Wed closed; Sat 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–21:00. Recheck before travelling, especially around holidays.
bestTime: Aim for an early lunch or early dinner to avoid the busiest meal period; December is Chiang Mai's cooler, popular travel season, so allow for a queue. Avoid Wednesday. Saturday has a dinner break between 15:00 and 17:00 per the listing.
gettingThere: At 24 Ratchaphruek Road, Chang Phueak, north-west of the old city. There is no rail transit in Chiang Mai; use a metered taxi, Grab/Bolt or songthaew and show the address in Thai/Maps. From the old city, allow roughly 10–20 minutes by road depending on traffic (estimate). Michelin lists a car park. Confirm the drop-off and parking arrangements with the driver.
booking: Michelin says the restaurant handles its own bookings and lists +66 98 261 8029. Call to ask about a December table, current menu, dietary needs and seating; some recent visitor comments report walk-in queues, so do not assume a reservation is available.
accessibility: Michelin confirms indoor air conditioning, outdoor tables and a garden, but gives no step-free entrance, wheelchair route, accessible toilet or mobility information. Contact the restaurant before going if access matters and request an indoor table if you need air conditioning; availability is unconfirmed.
practicalTips: For a first visit, share a Northern-style appetizer platter, then add one curry or soup and rice; ask staff which dishes are available that day.
Northern Thai dips and soups can be spicy. Ask for mild seasoning, but do not assume every dish can be adjusted.
Tell staff about allergies in simple terms and confirm ingredients directly; online sources do not provide a reliable allergen guide.
Carry some cash as backup even though Michelin lists credit cards accepted.
decemberNotes: The listed schedule is the current weekly schedule, not a guarantee for December 2026 holiday dates. Check directly a few days before visiting, and expect greater demand during the high season. No special December event or holiday hours were verified.
uncertainties: Exact December 2026 prices, menu availability and holiday hours may change; published menu prices are third-party listings and are not guaranteed current.
Vegetarian/vegan, halal, allergy and cross-contact accommodations are unverified.
Step-free access, seating layout and accessible toilet details are unverified.
